rounds.text: The valuation multiples applied to Aayush Art and Bullion Ltd are severely disconnected from fundamental reality, with the stock trading at an exorbitant P/E of 230x and a price-to-book ratio of 29.87x [E1, E2]. This extreme pricing leaves a massive negative margin of safety of -457.4%, as discounted cash flow models place intrinsic value at a mere Rs 213 per share against a market price of Rs 1,186 [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's price requires an unrealistic 42.7% earnings growth rate to justify itself, far eclipsing the base case assumption of 18.0% [E37]. Fundamental quality metrics fail to support this rich valuation, highlighted by a low median return on equity of just 8% over the last 5 years and high debtors averaging 167 days [E19, E57]. Cash generation is entirely disconnected from reported profitability, evidenced by an operating cash flow of Rs -0 Cr, a cash conversion ratio of -0.00x, and operating cash flow representing only 6% of operating profit in Mar 2026 [E26, E27, E29]. Insider alignment is deteriorating concurrently, with promoter holding dropping by 14.22 percentage points over recent years down to a low 24.63% by Mar 2026, while the company pays a 0.00% dividend [E4, E33, E58]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing compounded sales and profit growth alongside zero debt [E11, E15, E30].
